https://www.politico.eu/article/german-p.text: German police official Jürgen Ebner has been selected to become the next executive director of Europol, putting the longtime agency insider on track to lead Europe's increasingly powerful law enforcement body. EU ambassadors backed Ebner in a Council vote Wednesday, selecting the German from a three-person shortlist after weeks of horse-trading among national capitals. Ebner currently serves as Europol's deputy executive director for governance and has been acting executive director since Belgian Catherine De Bolle's mandate ended in May. He was widely regarded as De Bolle's right-hand man, making his selection a vote for continuity at The Hague-based agency. Advertisement Advertisement He beat two other senior police officials in the race: Alicia Malo, head of international cooperation at Spain's national police, and Linas Pernavas, director of Lithuania's main anti-corruption law enforcement agency. Ebner began his career with the German police in 1988 and went on to hold several operational positions at the Federal Criminal Police Office, or BKA, eventually serving in the office of its president. He moved to Europol in November 2019 after being appointed as deputy executive director responsible for governance. His portfolio has included legal and institutional matters, and he has also served as Europol's security coordinator. His selection does not quite finish the process. Ebner will now appear before the European Parliament's civil liberties committee, known as LIBE, which can issue a non-binding opinion on his candidacy. The Council of the EU will then formally appoint Europol's next executive director. He is set to take charge at a pivotal moment for the agency. The European Commission has proposed significantly expanding Europol's role, resources and technological capabilities as Brussels seeks a stronger response to organized crime, cyberattacks and hybrid threats. https://tribune.com.pk/story/2632033/bar.text: Home Entertainment Barbara Palvin and Dylan Sprouse announce birth of first baby The couple shared the news of their daughter's arrival with a photograph of the three watching the Dodgers play on TV Barbara Palvin and Dylan Sprouse have welcomed their first baby, the couple announced on Instagram on Monday, September 28. The model and actor shared the news through a collaborative Instagram post featuring a photograph of the couple watching the Dodgers play on television. Both were wearing Dodgers jerseys while holding their baby, who was facing away from the camera in a matching miniature jersey. “We took Labor Day literally this year.” Palvin also posted a closeup image of Sprouse holding their daughter on Instagram Stories with the caption, "Daddy's girl already 🧸 ". Photo: Instagram The couple have not yet revealed their daughter’s name. However, Sprouse previously confirmed that they were expecting a girl during an episode of his podcast, Wildmen , in July. “We’ve been calling her principessa…it’s Italian for princess,” Dylan said at the time. Palvin and Sprouse married in July 2023 on Palvin’s parents’ property in Hungary. The couple had previously announced that they were expecting their first child together, with the pregnancy marking a new chapter in their relationship. Based on the couple’s announcement and the timing of the US Labor Day holiday, their daughter may have been born on or around September 7, 2026. Their Instagram announcement offered fans a brief glimpse of their growing family through the Dodgers-themed photograph.
